title: Cover the platform tenant console with Playwright and make the picker spec assert usability
goal: The tenant console (TenantList, TenantOverview, TenantMemberList, TenantPlanEditor) has no automated UI coverage. The existing tenant specs cover the platform viewpoint header, cross-tenant isolation and the login picker, but not tenant CRUD, archive/delete, member add/remove, the ops overview or the plan editor. The login-picker spec is worse than uncovered: it builds a genuine multi-membership user, picks the tenant where the user has no roles, and asserts only that the app shell renders, which is exactly the failure mode (login succeeds, console is empty). This wave adds a console spec and strengthens the picker spec so it asserts a usable console or an explicit refusal, per the W3/W4 decision.
findings: TC-04 (P3): no e2e covers tenant create, edit, archive, delete, member add/remove, the ops overview or the plan editor; smoke-tenant is push-only and report-only.
The picker spec (tenant-hostile-browser-matrix.spec.ts:82-92, :138-140) constructs the cross-membership case but asserts only that .app-shell__header is visible, so the empty-menu outcome passes.
The console pages have no unit tests either, so a regression in TenantList/Overview/PlanEditor has no signal before release.

in: Add frontend/tests/smoke-core/tenant-console.spec.ts using the existing tenant-fixture helpers (setupMatrixTenants, teardownMatrixTenants, loginAsPlatformAdmin)

Cover: tenant list renders with summary cards; create a tenant with an admin; edit its name/plan; suspend and archive it; delete is unavailable before archived and succeeds after; deleted rows are absent from the default list
Cover: member add through the new user selector (W2) and member removal; the last-owner removal is refused with the documented error
Cover: tenant-ops overview numbers and the plan editor creating a custom code, assigning it to a tenant, and refusing to disable an in-use plan

Strengthen the login-picker spec: after the W4 decision, a cross-membership user either is not offered the unusable tenant, or switching there yields a working menu; assert the documented outcome and at least one protected API response, not just the shell

Add the new spec to the npm run test:smoke:tenant script in frontend/package.json (it currently lists tenant-hostile-browser-matrix, its phase2, tenant-protected-resources and the viewpoint spec) and to the smoke-tenant CI job; keep the job report-only unless the human gate approves making it blocking
Record the run command and the fixture prerequisites (tenantmatrixdb, seeded admin) in the spec header
out: Making smoke-tenant a required check without the maintainer's approval
Changing production source to make a test pass
Replacing the existing isolation or viewpoint specs
Testing the compatibility endpoints that W4 retains
Adding a new test runner or dependency

implementationNotes: The spec must create its own data and tear it down; do not depend on rows left by another spec.
Use the existing fixtures and helpers; if a helper is missing, add it to tenant-fixture.ts rather than duplicating login code.
The console delete test needs the W1 rule: create a tenant, assert delete is unavailable while active, archive it, then delete.
The plan-editor test must use a unique code per run (timestamp suffix) so reruns are idempotent.

The existing tenant specs need a live stack: scripts/run-smoke-suite.mjs starts Vite and scripts/tenant-matrix-fixture-setup.mjs provisions fixtures against a backend on 127.0.0.1:8080, which needs MySQL, Redis and a migrated database. Measured on 2026-10-27 12:40 with that stack up: the four existing specs ran 15 passed / 0 failed (matrix 10, viewpoint 5) in about 95s. Port 5173 was occupied by another dev server, so the suite was run on 5178 via the runner's --port flag; playwright takes baseURL from PANTHEON_WEB_BASE_URL, so no test change was needed. Fixtures must be torn down with tenant-matrix-fixture-setup.mjs down plus cleanup-smoke-fixtures.mjs, because the runner only calls setup up. Use the same recipe for the new console spec.
If a Playwright run is impossible in the executing environment, the wave still lands the spec and records not-run with the missing prerequisite; do not claim a green run.
A screenshot of the console before and after archive is the visual evidence; follow the project's existing capture helpers.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Write the spec against the shipped behaviour; if the UI lacks a stable selector, add an accessible role/label rather than a positional locator.
reviewerPosture: Confirm each test asserts an outcome, not just that a page rendered.
Confirm data is created and torn down per run.
Confirm the picker test now fails if the chosen tenant yields an empty menu.
Confirm the CI change only adds the spec to the existing job unless the gate was approved.
Confirm no production file changed to satisfy a locator.

commands: cd frontend && npx playwright test tests/smoke-core/tenant-console.spec.ts
runtimeEvidence: Playwright run output showing every new test passing against the local tenantmatrixdb fixture
screenshots of the tenant list before archive and after delete
if the environment is unavailable: not-run with the exact missing prerequisite

humanGates: Decide whether smoke-tenant becomes a blocking required check; the default is to add the spec while keeping the job report-only.
completionChecklist: Tenant console CRUD, archive/delete, members and plan editor have automated coverage
The login-picker spec no longer accepts an empty console as success
The new spec runs in the smoke-tenant job
The CI gate state is unchanged unless explicitly approved
No production source changed to satisfy a locator
